Islands & water

Cingkuak Island

Cingkuak Island is a small island in the Painan bay often reached as an extension from Pantai Carocok. This page separates stable background from access that must be confirmed at the jetty.

Updated · 28 Oktober 2026

Position

Island facing Painan

Cingkuak Island sits in the small island group facing Painan, not far from Pantai Carocok. From the beach edge, it appears as a point in the middle of the bay.

  • Visible from the edge of Pantai Carocok.
  • Reached by boat from the beach jetty.
  • Part of the Painan bay landscape, not a far separate landmass.

Background

Tower & local lore

The island is known for a watchtower remnant that is its visual signature from the beach. Some records mention a colonial-era origin, but we present the detail as general background, not verified fact.

Do not assume certain access

The tower is a visual feature; island entry, permits, and sea conditions must be confirmed with staff before planning a crossing.

Prepare

Before going

Keep buffer time and do not lock the crossing schedule. Read the boat and weather pages for conditions affecting the trip.

Questions

Before you go

01Is Cingkuak Island open to visitors?+

The island appears in the Painan bay view and is reached by boat, but today’s access status, permits, and crossing availability are unverified. Confirm at the jetty.

02Is there a tower on Cingkuak Island?+

The island has a watchtower that is its visual signature from the beach. Its historical detail varies in records; we present it as general background.

03How long is the crossing?+

Crossing time varies with operator and weather; we do not quote a fixed figure. Ask at the beach jetty.

04May I swim around the island?+

Water safety is set by sea conditions and staff guidance that day. Do not enter water when there is a restriction or warning.
